outcome: The Elliott–Halberstam conjecture itself (that primes have level of distribution 1-ε for every ε>0) remains open, with no movement on its own unconditional level-of-distribution bound (still bounded below Bombieri–Vinogradov's θ<1/2 plus the sieve-theoretic extensions already known before the frozen date). All activity found since 26 January 2024 is either a conditional/generalized variant, a related-but-distinct problem (bounded prime gaps), or a bare Lean formalization of the statement.
summary: I found no result that changes what a careful person would write in the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture's own entry (level of distribution θ = 1-ε for every ε>0, currently only known unconditionally for θ<1/2 via Bombieri–Vinogradov). Several adjacent things surfaced, all of which I judged out of scope under §3.1: (1) A November 2025 arXiv preprint (arxiv.org/abs/2511.14810, Trey Smith) proposes a 'Generalized Elliott-Halberstam Conjecture for Shifted Convolutions' (GEH-2), a distinct, stronger conjecture about correlations of the von Mangoldt function, and shows GEH-2 implies the twin prime conjecture. This changes a different statement, not this one — it is a related problem, not a case. (2) A ProofAtlas.ai collaboration page for this conjecture cites a 'Maynard 2025' well-factorable-weights result reaching moduli x^(3/5-ε); checking the citation (arXiv 2006.07088) shows this is actually a June 2020 paper — the page's date label is wrong, and in any case that result predates the frozen revision by years and was already reflected in the pre-2024 state of the art, so it is not a window event even under the correct date. (3) A July 2025 preprint by Thomas Wright (arXiv 2507.10780, 'Primes in Arithmetic Progressions to Large Moduli and Siegel Zeroes') obtains a conditional almost-all equidistribution result up to x^(2/3-ε), but only under a strong hypothetical exceptional character (Siegel zero) assumption — this is explicitly not an unconditional Elliott–Halberstam-type theorem, and an assumption of an exceptional character is itself a variant hypothesis, not a case of the stated conjecture. (4) A GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #3687), closed via PR #4459, formalized only the *statement* of the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture in Lean/Mathlib — the issue itself says it 'was generated by an AI agent and reviewed' by a human, but formalizing a statement (no proof, no bound moved) does not change the mathematics and is scoped out by §6.2's formalisation_only rule; ai_role is set to none because nothing mathematical resulted, and no proof-bearing claim exists to attach a basis_quote to. (5) Most substantively, in the narrow window of 31 August–3 September 2026 there was a burst of activity on the closely related but distinct problem of bounded gaps between primes (H₁): Julia Stadlmann proved H₁≤240 unconditionally (arXiv 2608.31126, 31 Aug 2026) by combining the Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem with existing (not new) equidistribution estimates for smooth moduli; Shiva Kintali then claimed H₁≤236 'with the help of AI' (1 Sep 2026, via social media, not yet a vetted paper); and the AI startup Axiom Math used a theorem-proving AI to push this to H₁≤212 within three days (3 Sep 2026), which IEEE Spectrum and other outlets covered as a machine-checkable formalization of what they called the 'BGP246'-descendant bound. A ScienceNews piece also reports OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra reaching H₁≤186 days later. All of this activity is about bounded gaps between primes, a different (if related and EH-adjacent) problem on Wikipedia's list, and none of it proves a new level-of-distribution / equidistribution estimate that would move the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture's own bound — Stadlmann's paper explicitly uses 'newer equidistribution estimates' that already existed rather than proving a new one. Under §3.1 this is squarely a related-problem cluster, not a case of Elliott–Halberstam, however much the same machinery (Bombieri–Vinogradov, sieve theory) is shared. I record it here only because it is the most substantial and heavily AI-involved event in the neighborhood of this conjecture, and because a future cross-check on the bounded-gaps-between-primes bullet should find it.
competing_reading: One could argue the Stadlmann/Kintali/Axiom Math/OpenAI activity belongs partly to this record because bounded gaps between primes is a direct, named consequence of the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture (EH implies gaps ≤6), and the same equidistribution machinery underlies both. But the conjecture as stated on this bullet is about the level of distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions, not about the numerical value of H₁, and none of the 2026 results proved a new equidistribution/level-of-distribution theorem — they combined existing ones. I judged this insufficient to count as a case of THIS problem, and it is the bounded-gaps-between-primes bullet's record (not this one) that should carry it as its primary event.
what_would_settle_it: A paper that either (a) proves an unconditional level-of-distribution result for primes in arithmetic progressions beyond θ<1/2 (or beyond whatever the pre-2024 sieve-theoretic ceiling was) without extra hypotheses, or (b) proves the Bombieri–Vinogradov-type estimate used in the 2026 bounded-gaps work is itself new (rather than a citation to prior work), would move this record from open to progress.
